subject: G-578-644 ATE safety follow-through and W4 checklist
body:
Dear monitoring team,

G-578-644 entered ATE at the placebo-controlled Week 24 visit on 03 Aug and attended ATE W4 on 31 Aug. All scheduled assessments were completed except urine pregnancy testing. AE source and EDC include onset, severity, nonserious status, relatedness, treatment, dose action and follow-up plan. Local safety labs were obtained. ECG was done with the study device and filed. No PK tube was collected; our lab worksheet had no research samples assigned because this was not a scheduled PK visit. She was available for phlebotomy and agreed to all requested bloods.

We called her 07 Sep: rash improving, continuing off drug per the PI/MM plan. She remains enrolled and will attend her planned visits.

Could you confirm whether you need a separate lab requisition for the unscheduled encounter?

Evelyn

The outside administration record is now attached.

All other criteria reviewed were satisfactory in both cases. We updated the history fields rather than opening new medical conditions. Please let me know if you need the discharge summary or just the neurology addendum for your review.

Regards,
Dr. Allen

Meg

subject: G-506-206 — nausea follow-up / unscheduled ATE assessment
body:
Dear monitoring team,

He called before taking that morning's drug. I discussed the case with the Medical Monitor that morning and we agreed to interrupt dosing while evaluating him.

He was assessed in clinic the same day, including an unscheduled PK sample, local chemistry, and ECG. No admission, immediate threat to life, persistent disability, or other SAE criterion was identified. I classified it as an expected, related, severe nonserious AE; nothing suggested a change to study conduct or new safety monitoring requirements. Full AE details and action on IP were entered in source and EDC that day.

Symptoms resolved 16 Sep. Following another discussion with the MM, he resumed two sticks/200 mg on 17 Sep. No change to the blind and no wish to leave the study. Study visits remain scheduled. We have not opened an ET or ordered a separate discontinuation safety call for this brief interruption.

Regards,
Priya Shah, MD
